articles.title: Some problems of recursive descent parsers (2009)
articles.summary: The recursive descent parser developed in the 2009 article by Eli Bendersky has a problem with operator associativity. The parser is built using a BNF (Backus-Naur Form) notation that defines the grammar for the parser, with the expr rule as an example. In this rule, the operator '-' is defined as a binary operator that takes two terms and produces a result. However, the associativity of the '-' operator is not left-associative, but rather right-associative, causing problems for subtraction and division. The parser's wheeling behavior can lead to an infinite loop, resulting in incorrect results.
